summary:
In places like Alicante, Spain, climate change has made agriculture a complete gamble. With uncertain droughts and heat waves, farmers have to make use of their old-fashioned instincts and may plant crops that are destined to fail for subsidies.

The objective here is to safeguard the farmers and their businesses before the actual planting. Our product is called OutWeather, a novel technology which transforms the approach from predicting weather to protecting against it. Although it’s impossible to predict the amount of rainfall next year, OutWeather analyzes decades of NASA’s earth observation data for specific farmer’s plot to run stress test of crop rotations based on historical weather extremes and 2050 projections.

Proactive protection of crops is its main innovation. It helps to find combinations of crops which naturally save water, enrich soil and defend crops against the effects of climate extremes. Solving the problem of transforming space data into local protection, OutWeather provides farmers with protection instead of the blind annual gamble.
details:
OUTWEATHER

OutWeather is a full-stack application that combines NASA Earth-observation data, agronomic modeling, and climate projections to stress-test crop rotations before a single seed goes into the ground. The system ingests over 20 years of satellite and ground data that includes GPM IMERG precipitation, NASA POWER daily meteorology, SMAP root-zone soil moisture, MODIS vegetation indices, and USDA SSURGO soil profiles. Once a user draws their parcel boundary on the satellite map, our engine evaluates candidate crop rotations against past droughts, heat waves, late frost, and FAO GAEZ 2050 climate scenarios using FAO-56 water balance and FAO-33 yield response models.

The benefits are resilience and transparency: traditional farm planning relies solely on the preceding year's weather, turning each season into a high-stakes bet. In places like Alicante, Spain, extreme climate volatility has driven farmers to sow cereal, knowing they would lose the harvest simply to retain subsidies. OutWeather cuts crop failure risk, reduces peak irrigation demand by up to 22%, and attaches full data provenance to every figure, eliminating the distrust associated with black-box tools.

We built the project with Next.js 15, TypeScript, Three.js (3D), Leaflet and MapLibre, alongside a modular Python backend (FastAPI, NumPy, SQLite, and Docker). The system features an offline-first architecture with deterministic data fixtures, ensuring simulations execute in under 90 seconds even without an active internet connection.

The project is creative because it transforms complex satellite data into an intuitive, explainable, and actionable rehearsal of multiple futures. We balanced scientific rigor with practical usability, delivering not just raw analytics but an interactive 3D parcel viewer, editable rotation timelines, monthly disease risk calendars, hazard emergency protocols, and automated PDF and CSV reports.
